RULES.currentRule: Absentee ballots are limited to voters who meet a qualifying reason (illness, disability, absence from the municipality, etc.). Voters who don't need a reason should use a mail-in ballot.
RULES.whyItMatters: Distinguishes the two PA mail-voting tracks and which application a voter should use.

RULES.currentRule: Mail-in and absentee ballot applications must be received by the county election office by 5:00 PM seven days before election day.

RULES.whyItMatters: Defines the window for in-person voting in PA-07.

RULES.topic: Voter ID / first-time voter ID (photo NOT required; non-photo IDs also accepted)
RULES.currentRule: In Pennsylvania, voters do NOT need to show photo identification at the polling place. Poll workers should not ask every voter for photo identification. ID is required ONLY the first time a voter casts a ballot in an election district — either a first-time voter or a voter voting at a new polling place for the first time. Those voters may show either photo OR non-photo ID. Photo IDs accepted include: PA driver's license or PennDOT ID card, ID issued by any Commonwealth agency, ID issued by the U.S. Government, U.S. passport, U.S. Armed Forces ID, student ID (including electronic/digital student ID), or employee ID. Non-photo IDs with the voter's name and address accepted include: voter registration card issued by the county voter registration office, non-photo ID issued by the U.S. Government, non-photo ID issued by any agency of the Commonwealth or U.S. Government, firearm permit, current utility bill, current bank statement, paycheck, or government check. Returning voters at their established polling place generally do not need to show ID.
RULES.whyItMatters: Affects in-person eligibility for first-time voters or those voting at a new polling place for the first time in the district (Lehigh, Northampton, Monroe, and Carbon counties). Photo ID is not required; a wide range of non-photo IDs bearing name and address are also acceptable, and framing ID as photo-only can discourage eligible voters.
RULES.detail: Per PA Department of State 'Voter Identification Requirements for Voting' guidance (Sept. 22, 2025) and 25 P.S. § 3050(a). The photo-ID law passed in 2012 (Act 18 of 2012) was struck down by Commonwealth Court in 2014 (Applewhite v. Commonwealth) and the Commonwealth did not appeal; the first-time-voter ID requirement in HAVA and 25 P.S. § 3050(a) remains in effect for the November 3, 2026 election.

RULES.topic: Mail-in / absentee ballot APPLICATION identification requirements
RULES.currentRule: When applying for a mail-in or absentee ballot, PA voters must provide proof of identification following a cascade: (1) If the voter has a valid, current Pennsylvania driver's license or PennDOT ID card, the voter must provide the license/ID number. (2) If the voter does NOT have a PA driver's license or PennDOT ID card, the voter must provide the last 4 digits of their Social Security number. (3) Only if the voter has neither may the voter provide a photocopy of an approved photo ID with a current expiration date. Approved photocopy IDs are limited to: U.S. passport, U.S. military ID (active duty and retired military ID may have an indefinite expiration; military dependents' ID must be current), federal / Pennsylvania / PA-county / PA-municipal government employee photo ID, photo ID from an accredited PA public or private higher-education institution, or photo ID from a PA care facility (including long-term-care, assisted-living, and personal-care homes). Voters covered by UOCAVA (uniformed and overseas) or the Voting Accessibility for the Elderly and Handicapped Act (VAEH) are exempt from these ID requirements. If a voter forgets ID with the application, the county still sends a ballot but the voter has SIX (6) CALENDAR DAYS after the election to provide proof of identification.
RULES.whyItMatters: Mail-in and absentee ballot APPLICATIONS require ID at the application stage, not just at the ballot-return stage. Voters who lack a PA driver's license or PennDOT ID commonly overlook the SSN4 option and mistakenly send a photocopy. Voters who forget ID entirely still receive a ballot and have 6 calendar days after the election to cure the deficiency.
RULES.detail: Per PA Department of State 'Voter Identification Requirements for Voting' guidance (Sept. 22, 2025), 25 Pa.C.S. § 3146.2b(b) (absentee) and § 3150.12b(b) (mail-in), and Act 77 of 2019. The 6-calendar-day post-election ID cure window is set by DOS guidance following the 2020 litigation over Boockvar guidance; voters who fail to cure by that deadline have their ballots rejected.

RULES.currentRule: Pennsylvania law requires voters to handwrite a date on the mail-ballot outer envelope. Whether undated or misdated envelopes are counted has been the subject of ongoing litigation.
RULES.whyItMatters: Affects whether a returned mail ballot is counted in close PA-07 contests.
RULES.detail: Watch item — see Conflicts panel. Spotlight PA explainer and PA Department of State guidance should be reconciled before public reliance.

RULES.currentRule: Voters can track their mail-in or absentee ballot status through PA Voter Services from application through receipt at the county election office.
RULES.whyItMatters: Lets voters confirm their ballot was received in time and resolve issues before deadlines.

RULES.currentRule: Pennsylvania elections are administered at the county level. Mail-in and absentee applications, ballots, and in-person logistics flow through each county's election office.
RULES.whyItMatters: PA-07 voters interact with Carbon, Lehigh, Northampton, or Monroe county election offices depending on residence.

RULES.currentRule: PA-07 includes all of Carbon, Lehigh, and Northampton counties and parts of Monroe County under the maps used for the 2022–2030 cycle.
RULES.whyItMatters: Determines who is a constituent of PA-07.

UPDATES.title: SCOTUS denied RNC emergency request on PA provisional-ballot backstop (June 6, 2026)

Denial was procedural — the case (limited to two voters in one county) was not a proper vehicle for statewide relief. Justices Alito, Thomas, and Gorsuch wrote separately leaving the underlying constitutional question open. The Coalfield Justice provisional-ballot backstop remains operative for November 3, 2026.

NEWS.headline: SCOTUS responses due June 1 in PA mail-ballot dating case — ruling could affect November
NEWS.relevanceSummary: Responses in Commonwealth v. Eakin (No. 25-967) were due at SCOTUS on June 1, 2026. If the Court takes the case and reverses the 3rd Circuit, counties may again be allowed to reject undated mail ballots — directly affecting PA-07 general election mail voters.

NEWS.headline: Bob Brooks wins Democratic nomination in hotly contested PA-07 primary
NEWS.relevanceSummary: Bob Brooks (D), president of the PA Fire Fighters Association and Gov. Shapiro's preferred candidate, won the May 19 Democratic primary for PA-07 with 41.4% of the vote. Ryan Mackenzie (R) advances as the Republican nominee. Brooks vs. Mackenzie is the November 3 general election matchup.

NEWS.headline: PA's 2026 primary election goes well despite a few isolated incidents
NEWS.relevanceSummary: Statewide primary ran without major machine malfunctions or printing errors. Isolated incidents in York and Chester counties affected a few hundred voters but did not disrupt statewide results. Turnout was low — under 20% of registered voters.

NEWS.headline: Uncertainty for PA counties after court rules on releasing vote data
NEWS.relevanceSummary: PA Supreme Court unanimously ruled CVRs are public records (April 2026, Heather Honey v. Lycoming County). But how many PA counties can actually release them depends on tabulation technology — only 8 counties use Clear Ballot systems with ballot randomization. Lehigh and Northampton (PA-07 counties) may face different timelines.

NEWS.headline: SCOTUS denies RNC emergency request to block PA provisional-ballot backstop
NEWS.relevanceSummary: On June 6, 2026, SCOTUS denied the RNC's emergency request to stop PA from counting provisional ballots from voters whose mail-in ballots had envelope errors. Denial was procedural (case was limited to two voters in one county). Alito/Thomas/Gorsuch wrote separately leaving the constitutional question open.

NEWS.headline: Judge blocks USPS proposed restrictions on mail-in voting
NEWS.relevanceSummary: A federal judge blocked proposed USPS restrictions that would have affected how mail ballots are delivered and handled nationwide. Because the article says the proposal would have required states to adopt new ballot procedures before deliveries, it matters to PA-07 voters who use mail ballots.

NEWS.headline: Voter roll purges banned 90 days before federal elections
NEWS.relevanceSummary: This explains a federal quiet-period rule that limits systematic voter-roll removals in the 90 days before federal elections. It is relevant to Pennsylvania voters because the article says the National Voter Registration Act applies to Pennsylvania and other covered states, and the Supreme Court is set to review a case that could narrow that protection.

NEWS.headline: Voting Rights Groups Secure Legal Win for Pennsylvania Voter Privacy
NEWS.relevanceSummary: The League says a federal judge dismissed a U.S. Department of Justice effort to obtain Pennsylvania voter data, preserving voter privacy protections. That matters to PA-07 voters because it concerns election administration in Pennsylvania and the handling of voter-registration records.

NEWS.headline: Supreme Court asks Trump administration views on Pennsylvania mail-in ballot date requirement
NEWS.relevanceSummary: This concerns Pennsylvania’s mail-in ballot envelope-date rule, which directly affects whether ballots are counted in the state. Reuters says the Supreme Court asked for the administration’s views on a Republican bid to enforce the handwritten date requirement, a procedural issue PA-07 mail voters should watch.

NEWS.headline: Trump Justice Department can't have Pennsylvania voters' private information, judge says
NEWS.relevanceSummary: Votebeat reports that a federal judge dismissed a DOJ lawsuit seeking Pennsylvania voters’ private information, a direct election-administration issue. PA-07 voters have an interest because the ruling affects how state voter-roll data is protected and managed.

NEWS.headline: PA voting laws could change if Democrats win 2026 elections
NEWS.relevanceSummary: Spotlight PA reports that if Democrats secure a governing trifecta in Harrisburg, they are poised to advance changes to election law such as expanded pre-canvassing of mail ballots and codifying key court rulings, which would directly affect statewide voting procedures for PA-07 voters.[2]

NEWS.headline: With data centers in mind, Pa. House votes to close Sunshine Act loophole after court ruling
NEWS.relevanceSummary: PennLive reports that the Pennsylvania House overwhelmingly approved a bill to tighten the Sunshine Act by limiting when public bodies can add agenda items less than 24 hours before meetings, improving transparency in official decision-making, including actions by county election boards that affect PA-07 voters.[7]

NEWS.headline: Pa. House passes ‘pre-canvassing’ bill that would speed up election results
NEWS.relevanceSummary: The Pennsylvania House passed a bill to allow county officials to begin pre-canvassing mail-in ballots one week before Election Day, which would change how ballots are processed and how quickly results are reported for all voters, including those in PA-07.[3]

NEWS.headline: Election laws still point of debate in Pennsylvania
NEWS.relevanceSummary: This article reviews ongoing political and legal disputes over Pennsylvania’s election laws, referencing past state Supreme Court rulings on congressional maps and the Free and Equal Elections Clause, which frame current and future redistricting and election-law debates affecting districts like PA-07.[4]

NEWS.headline: Adjust Mail-In Ballot Application Deadline and Extend Pre-Canvass Period: Luzerne County recommendations
NEWS.relevanceSummary: Luzerne County officials outline proposed changes to Pennsylvania’s Election Code, including moving the mail-in ballot application deadline from 7 to 14 days before elections and lengthening the pre-canvass period, reforms that would apply statewide and influence mail voting logistics for PA-07 if enacted.[8]

NEWS.headline: How to Vote in Erie County: Polling hours and mail ballot return
NEWS.relevanceSummary: Erie County’s guidance details standard Pennsylvania procedures for polling hours, in-line voting rights, and contacting county officials about registration, illustrating county-level election administration practices that mirror those used in other counties statewide, including those that comprise PA-07.[6]

NEWS.headline: Voting and Election Information in Pennsylvania
NEWS.relevanceSummary: The Attorney General’s updated voter guidance explains current statewide rules on polling-place challenges, provisional ballots, and critical mail-in ballot requirements—such as using the secrecy envelope and properly signing and dating the return envelope—which directly govern how PA-07 voters must cast valid ballots.[1]

NEWS.headline: Can Pa. elections officials get approval to sort mail ballots earlier?
NEWS.relevanceSummary: This article explains proposed statewide legislation that would allow Pennsylvania counties to begin sorting and opening mail ballots up to seven days before Election Day, potentially affecting how quickly results are reported and how mail-in ballots are handled for all voters, including those in PA-07.

NEWS.headline: Pa. Republicans in Congress stay quiet on Trump’s new ‘Save America Act’ targeting elections
NEWS.relevanceSummary: The article explains that the proposed federal 'Save America Act' would require voters to provide proof of citizenship when registering and to show photo ID at the polls, changes that would directly alter voter-registration and voter-ID procedures for all Pennsylvania voters if enacted.

NEWS.headline: McCormick, Pa. GOP push voter ID bill but don’t challenge Trump’s 2020 fraud claims
NEWS.relevanceSummary: This article explains Pennsylvania Republicans’ support for the federal SAVE America Act, which would require proof of citizenship to register and photo ID to vote, and would scale back mail voting—changes that would directly alter voter registration, in‑person ID rules, and mail‑in ballot access for all Pennsylvania voters, including those in PA‑07.[1][8]

NEWS.headline: Shapiro responds to Trump, DHS claims on noncitizens on Pa. voter rolls
NEWS.relevanceSummary: This statewide piece details DHS claims about noncitizens on Pennsylvania’s voter rolls and the response from Gov. Shapiro and Secretary of the Commonwealth Al Schmidt, who emphasize existing voter‑verification requirements at registration, for mail voting, and when voting at a new polling place—procedures that govern how PA‑07 voters register and cast ballots.[2]

NEWS.headline: Pennsylvania
NEWS.relevanceSummary: This updated voter resource explains Pennsylvania’s voter‑ID rules, including that ID is generally required only the first time a voter casts a ballot in a precinct, lists accepted photo and non‑photo IDs, and details ID number and ID‑copy requirements when requesting mail‑in or absentee ballots—directly guiding PA‑07 voters on how to comply with ID and mail‑ballot procedures.[12]

NEWS.headline: Legislative Update: PennDOT document privacy and Office of Open Records appeal changes
NEWS.relevanceSummary: This legislative update notes a planned bill to limit PennDOT’s disclosure of documents used to obtain driver’s licenses or ID cards and explains new filing rules for appeals to the Office of Open Records; changes to ID document privacy and access could affect how voter‑ID records are handled and how election‑related public records are challenged statewide, including in PA‑07.[14]

NEWS.headline: 5 Senators Press Thune on SAVE America Act as Voter Roll Cleanup Costs Dems 9,000 in Pennsylvania
NEWS.relevanceSummary: The article discusses federal proposals affecting voter roll maintenance and notes that recent voter roll cleanup in Pennsylvania removed thousands of registrations, highlighting ongoing changes and scrutiny around registration records that impact how voters statewide, including in PA-07, stay registered and ensure their status is current.[6]

NEWS.headline: Pennsylvania Green Party warns of unauthorized ballot effort in House races
NEWS.relevanceSummary: The story reports that the Pennsylvania Green Party is warning about an unauthorized effort to place candidates on the ballot in U.S. House races, raising questions about ballot-access procedures and candidate qualification that could affect general-election ballots seen by voters in districts such as PA-07.[8]

NEWS.headline: Former Pa. Gov. Corbett co-authors column criticizing fellow Republicans' SAVE Act
NEWS.relevanceSummary: This coverage of debate around the federal SAVE Act involves Pennsylvania election policy discussions, touching on how proposed federal requirements for proof of citizenship and voter-roll verification could interact with state-level voter registration and identification procedures affecting Pennsylvania voters, including those in PA-07.[14]

NEWS.headline: How the G.O.P. Turned Olive Garden Into a Voter ID Talking Point
NEWS.relevanceSummary: This article examines Republican messaging around voter ID and the SAVE America Act, which includes provisions on voter identification and proof of citizenship that could reshape ID requirements for registration and voting nationwide, including for Pennsylvania voters if enacted.[10]
